name: CHURCH & MEETING HALL
materialIdentity: Whitewashed plank under open rafters, honey wood, wall lamps, night (errata 90 A)
note: Room 17, doc 20. Reached by the map; THE DOOR, ALWAYS UNLOCKED leads back to it. Lines EXTRACTED from docs/05, 09, 54 and 49 by tools/extract-examine.mjs and compiled by tools/compile-room.mjs. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

generated.note: GENERATED. Edit the documents or the annotation, never this file.

entrances.note: In by the door, at left: the map leads here.

LOOK_AT.say: Brass, dented, honest. It has held buttons, promissory notes, and once, famously, a nugget nobody would afterward claim.
repeat: Empty, and polished. It has been polished a great deal more than it has been filled.
Somebody has scratched a small cross on the rim and somebody else a small dollar sign, and both have been polished over equally.

LISTEN_TO.say: A ring when set down. It sounds fuller than it is, which is a kindness.
repeat: Nothing.
A last ring as the plate settles on its bolt. Fuller than it is, again.

overrides.PICK_UP: It is bolted down, which I take to be doctrine informed by experience.

LOOK_AT.say: The hymnal, one copy per pew, tuned to whatever key the congregation reaches by verse two. There are pencil corrections in mine. They are wrong, but devout.
repeat: Somebody has pressed a flower in Hymn 41. It has outlasted whoever meant it.
Every hymn has its key printed at the top. Not one of them is the key this town sings in.

LISTEN_TO.say: Pages. A soft chord of paper.
repeat: Nothing. Nobody opens it. They sing what they remember, and they remember it wrong, and they remember it wrong together, which is nearly as good.
Nothing. It is waiting for Sunday, when it will be overruled.

overrides.USE: I corrected the penciled corrections. Somebody has since corrected mine. The hymnal is now a debate.

LOOK_AT.say: You cannot see it from here. You can see where the ceiling knows about it.
repeat: A dark ring on the ceiling boards around the hole, where years of ringing have shaken the dust loose.
I have never seen it and I could draw you its crack.

LISTEN_TO.say: A half-step flat, even in memory.
repeat: Nothing at the moment, and I can still hear exactly how wrong it is.
The beam it hangs from ticks in the heat. The bell is saving its error for the morning.

LOOK_AT.say: Who paid for what. The Colonel paid for the roof, the windows, the bell, and the stove, and his name is on all four in gilt.
repeat: The Colonel's name is in gilt four times. Everyone else's is in ink once, and some have been crossed out and written in again, smaller.
At the bottom, in pencil: ORGAN FUND — $3.15. It has been $3.15 for some years.
Nothing. Gratitude, framed and hung, makes no sound.
The frame tapping the wall when the door goes. The Colonel, knocking politely.

LOOK_AT.say: SERVICES SUNDAY. FUNERALS AS REQUIRED. A schedule of fees below, in a smaller hand.
repeat: The fees are by the word, and the longer words cost more.
WEDDINGS has been painted out. There is room under it for something new, and nothing has been put there.
The pin rattling in the draft from the door.
Nothing. A schedule with one fixed day has very little to say.

LOOK_AT.say: The rope drops through a hole in the ceiling from the only bell in the district.
repeat: A rope, going up through a hole in the ceiling to the flattest bell in the territory.
A second knot is tied higher up, for a taller ringer. Nobody has needed it since Sowerby came.
then: Frayed at pulling height by six years of Reverend Sowerby's mornings.

LISTEN_TO.say: The rope creaks against the beam. The bell above holds its breath.
repeat: Nothing, at rest. It is the only time it is bearable.
A faint hum down the rope from above. The bell is never entirely silent; it is only flat quietly.

overrides.PULL: The whole town orders its morning by that flat note, and it was not morning. Sowerby appeared before the echo died. We have agreed it was the wind.

LOOK_AT.say: Built tall by a carpenter who admired authority.
repeat: There is a step behind it for a shorter preacher. Sowerby uses neither.
On the shelf inside, a sermon in Sowerby's hand, priced in the margin.
then: Sowerby preaches from beside it, which the carpenter would have taken hard.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. It keeps the sermons it was promised.
repeat: The boards behind it creak when the door opens, as though someone were about to begin.
Nothing. A pulpit nobody climbs is the quietest furniture in town.

overrides.USE: I stood at it a moment while the hall was empty. It faces a room of chairs the way my claim faces the future: expectantly, on faith.

LOOK_AT.say: Plain glass, no colors. The territory does its own stained glass at dawn and dusk, and the church accepts the donation.
repeat: Real glass, freighted four hundred miles. The single most expensive object in Consolation, and it looks out at mud.
There is a bubble in one pane, low in the corner. The whole street bends around it a little, like a congregation around a stranger.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wind. The glass thins it into something nearly sung.
repeat: Nothing.
The wind again, nearly sung. It never quite reaches the note.

LOOK_AT.say: A stove that heats the near half of the room.
repeat: Gilt letters on the door: GIVEN BY COL. A. FANSHAWE. Even the stove is grateful in public.
The front pews have their paint blistered from it and the back pews have frost in January. Theology, by distance.
then: Salvation, like heat, reaches the back pews late.

LISTEN_TO.say: Ticking iron. It preaches in the cold months.
repeat: A slow tick as it cools, like a clock with nothing to count.
Nothing. Cold iron, waiting for the cold months to give it something to say.

overrides.TALK_TO: I asked it to extend its range to the back pews. It ticked noncommittally, like everything else in this building with a congregation.

LOOK_AT.say: Eight pews, benched close. On Sundays the whole town fits in here, which tells you something about the size of the town and something about Sundays.
repeat: Pews built from the crates the piano came in. The third one still reads PROVIDENCE R I, which is where I am from. I have sat down.
The back pew is worn smoother than the front. The town's devotion is strongest nearest the door.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wood, easing. Six days of quiet with one loud one coming.
repeat: Nothing.
A pew creaking under nobody. Old wood remembering a Sunday.

LOOK_AT.say: Boards, laid properly, tongued and grooved. Somebody built this building to last and every other building on this street to sell.
repeat: A worn path runs from the door to the stove and another from the stove to the door. The pews are mostly decorative.
Not a nail head standing proud in the whole floor. Whoever laid it believed in something.

LISTEN_TO.say: Solid underfoot. Not a creak in it, which in this town is a kind of miracle.
repeat: My own footsteps, sounding more certain than I feel.
Nothing. It was built to be quiet, and it is.

LOOK_AT.say: The hall's other life: a long table where the town votes on things it has already decided at the Nugget.
repeat: Rings from coffee cups at one end and from whiskey glasses at the other. The town divides along the table.
The minutes book lies open at the last meeting. Item one: the Company's proposal. Carried. Item two: nothing.

LISTEN_TO.say: A wobble in one leg. Democracy, structurally.
repeat: The wobble again when I lean on it. The motion is seconded.
Nothing. The town is not in session.

exits.name: THE DOOR, ALWAYS UNLOCKED

LOOK_AT.say: No lock on a church door, Sowerby says, and no hinge oiled either — so the door announces every sinner at full volume.
repeat: The hinge pin has been tapped half out and tapped back in. Somebody tried to oil it and was overruled.
It stands open more than it is shut. Sowerby says a church should be easy to enter. He says nothing about leaving.
The hinge, as I pass. It has my name ready.
The street through the gap, and the hinge waiting to comment on whoever comes next.

exits.note: Doc 20: the church is reached by the map, and its door leads back to it. Doc 05 and doc 54 write the door's LOOK and LISTEN.

PICK_UP.say: There would be a charge. There is a charge for everything here, including, I suspect, the suggestion.

PUSH.say: He would bless me for it, at the standard rate.

USE.say: He is available, by the word.
